attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, with no hedging.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the sentence: $12B is less than one quarter of OpenAI's compute costs. It is a firm statement about current cost levels.

contract.note: The sentence names no quarter. Anchoring to Q1 2026, as the post's own cost discussion does, is an ordinary reading. Requiring a compute-only total rather than cash burn or R&D is fair.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no admissible evidence items. The Information was inaccessible, Reuters covers cash burn rather than compute expense, and the $12.1B figure traces back to Zitron himself. No independent Q1 2026 compute total is in the packet, so the claim cannot be settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, building on analyst estimates he cites. The conclusion is his.

semantics.note: The capacity antecedent, the threshold of over $147B and the horizon through end-2027 are kept. The proposition drops 'expected' and 'just', but this does not change what is scored.

contract.note: Limiting the count to the four named providers and excluding the costs he lists as excluded follows his text. The July 2026 start is inferred from his year-and-a-half framing, which is reasonable.

evidence.note: A real OpenAI disclosure of a $100B, eight-year AWS expansion. It gives no payment schedule for the window, says nothing about the other providers, and does not show the capacity condition was met.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2027-12-31, after the evaluation date. Whether the capacity antecedent holds is unknown, and the early-resolution rule has not been met. The only evidence item is context.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Dropping the CEO remark as opinion is right. Identifying the competitor as Anthropic follows the context. Reading 'revenues are slowing' as slowing growth is fair.

contract.note: The result depends on how 'slowing' and 'outpaced' are read and on the year-to-date window. The contract's readings are ordinary and it records the alternatives.

evidence.note: Covers combined growth for both labs only, says 'may be slowing', and warns its figures are imprecise. It does not show either company slowing on its own.
Shows Anthropic ahead ($65B vs $40B) even allowing for accounting differences, but is dated after the window. It bears on 'outpaced' only and says nothing about slowing.
Bloomberg, Aug 14, citing anonymous sources: OpenAI revenue 'accelerated in recent months'. This runs against the slowing claim, though it is not a consistent dated series.

reviews.rationale: Anthropic's lead in run rate looks plausible on e2 but falls outside the window. For OpenAI, e3 reports acceleration, which counts against slowing, yet the contract requires at least three consistently measured observations per company, and the packet has neither those nor a reconciled series. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The firm part is 'at least 20%'. The '30-40%' part is hedged and is rightly treated as tentative and unscored. The profitability remark is set aside correctly.

contract.note: Comparing commitments with matching projected cloud revenue is the ordinary reading. The Q2 2026 reference quarter is somewhat artificial, but it does not change the result. Provider set and period are unspecified.

evidence.note: One AWS commitment, with no annual allocation, no other providers and no matching revenue denominator.
Historical Q2 2026 cloud market size and shares. It is not a forecast and says nothing about OpenAI's share of future revenue.

reviews.rationale: Testing the ratio needs a full schedule of OpenAI's commitments and a matching forecast of the providers' cloud revenue. The packet has neither, and its two items are context only, so the 20% threshold can be neither confirmed nor refuted.
